name: Ground-contact point

phase_0.boundary_condition: The mechanical interface between a rigid or elastic body and a supporting substrate.

VINIT.justification: The state of the body in free motion before the boundary condition of the ground is established.

TANCH.justification: The terminal constraint that limits the downward displacement of the system.

AFWD.justification: The forward transformation of the material under load toward the ground.

AREV.justification: The reverse transformation where stored energy returns the material toward its original state.

CLINK.justification: The sequential chaining of force from the center of mass through the structure to the contact patch.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-recognition of the body's shape as it conforms to the ground topology.

FSPLIT.justification: The split of the total contact force into normal force and tangential friction.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of normal and tangential components into a single vector acting on the body.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where the ground successfully supports the load without slip.

EVALF.justification: The failure state where tangential force exceeds friction, resulting in displacement.

ENGAGR.justification: The paradice state where the system is simultaneously at rest and at the threshold of sliding.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, irreversible record of the contact event on the material surface.

phase_3.void_description: Airborne state with zero ground reaction force.
phase_3.true_description: Stable contact with zero relative velocity.
phase_3.false_description: Loss of contact or uncontrolled sliding.
phase_3.both_description: Stick-slip oscillation where the system transitions rapidly between states.

steps.domain_action: Body approaches the ground plane from a state of free motion.
Gravitational acceleration drives the body toward the terminal boundary.
The ground plane establishes the spatial limit of the system.
The material interface recognizes the ground topology and defines the contact patch.
Internal stresses chain from the core to the contact interface.
The contact force differentiates into vertical support and horizontal resistance.
The normal force successfully counters gravity, establishing a T-state.
The material undergoes elastic deformation in response to the normal load.
The tangential load is assessed against the friction coefficient.
At the limit of static friction, the system holds both stick and slip potentials.
The normal and frictional components reintegrate into the total ground reaction force.
Micro-abrasions record the mechanical history of the contact event.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The laws of classical mechanics translating mass and acceleration into force.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Stress wave propagation through the molecular lattice of the material.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Elastic potential energy stored within the molecular bonds of the contact zone.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The time-step of the physical interaction, governed by the speed of sound in the material.
phase_5.alfs_store: The material constant library defining Young's modulus and friction coefficients.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Heat generated by internal friction and molecular deformation.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Potential energy of the body relative to the ground.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Thermal energy dissipated into the substrate and body.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The cycle is nearly conservative in the elastic regime where deformation is recovered.
